in Ordinary Time September 27 2026 Renovation Updates The End is Nigh This past Tuesday we were scheduled for our punch list walk through with our team from Shawnee Construction For the second time however this walk through was cancelled and rescheduled for this coming week As this walk through is necessary to identify any remaining incomplete damaged or incorrect work that must be fixed before closing out our project this additional delay is another unexpected setback in our schedule This means that our hope to be fully back in the sanctuary by next weekend will most likely not be met This hope was contingent on the walk through having occurred this past Tuesday which would allow nearly two weeks for any needed work to be completed With this additional delay we will remain in our continuing arrangement for just a bit longer bit inconvenient yes But better for the work to be done correctly than quickly In Deuteronomy 341 4 we hear how Moses sees the Promised Land atop Mount Nebo In this moment we are spiritually united with Moses With the removal of the dust screen this past Monday we can now peak around the veil and see the beauty of the work being completed even as we cannot yet enter that sacred space Instead we are being given the opportunity to grow in patience until we receive the all clear to reenter the sanctuary Liturgical and Altar Arrangements As we continue to prepare for Masses to resume in the sanctuary I have been contemplating our use of liturgical arrangements over the past few months Since January our daily Masses have made use of the ad orientem altar arrangement Likewise the same has been true for our weekend Masses since the sanctuary flooring work began in July Prior to this we exclusively used the versus populum altar arrangement at all Masses In one of his last apostolic letters Pope Francis reminded us that every aspect of the liturgical celebration must be carefully tended to space time gestures words objects vestments song music The reason for such care he explains is so that the faithful are not robbed of what is owed to them the Paschal Mystery celebrated according to the ritual that the Church sets down Desiderio desideravi Para 23 Taking this sentiment of our late Holy Father Pope Francis into account with an understanding that the richness of the Church does allow for both altar arrangements I would like to make room for both in our regular liturgical schedule We generally offer nine Masses each week three weekend Masses and six weekdays I am considering that one weekend and one weekday Mass will be offered ad orientem and the remaining seven Masses versus populum Looking at our current schedule I am leaning towards our 8:30AM Friday daily Mass and 10 AM Sunday weekend Mass being the two Masses offered ad orientem and our five other daily Masses and 5 PM Saturday Vigil and 7:30AM Sunday weekend Masses offered versus populum This allows variety to our liturgical schedule and multiple options for personal preference One thing to keep in mind with personal preference is that it is exactly that a preference We may find certain liturgical practices helpful to our prayer life but this does not make other practices right or wrong The Church permits a variety of practices My hope is that we can approach both arrangements with the care that the Church asks of us with patience toward one another and our attention ultimately fixed on the Lord whom we have come to worship Stuff the Truck St Vincent de Paul Society Next weekend October 3rd 4th we will be partnering with the St Vincent de Paul Society of Decatur for a Stuff the Truck event This event helps to support the St Vincent de Paul Thrift Store Ministry of our neighboring parish St Mary of the Assumption in nearby Decatur to provide clothing and furniture for those in need There will be a bulletin insert next weekend with more information regarding donations what is being asked for etc Saturday September 26 400 4:45pm
